title: Spatiotemporal patterns of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and associations with local infrastructure and land use in South Korea, 2011–2024 (analysis code and compiled data)
description: Reproducibility package for a Bayesian spatiotemporal analysis of district-level hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) incidence across 228 South Korean districts, 2011-2024 (3,192 district-years, 5,634 notified cases): negative-binomial model with age-standardized expected counts as offset, BYM2 spatial effect, first-order random-walk year effect and district-year interaction, fitted with R-INLA. Contains the R scripts for the 19-covariate principal model, the period-specific refits (2011-2015, 2016-2019, 2020-2024), the urban-share adjustment, and the sensitivity program (imputation exclusion, likelihood and random-effect structure, compositional land-use coding, eight neighbourhood graphs, alternative priors, zero-inflated likelihood, pandemic-year specifications, healthcare-access removal), residual and posterior predictive diagnostics, the compiled district-year analysis panel with a variable codebook, the neighbourhood graph and district boundaries, archived manuscript values, and R/INLA session information. The covariate specification was developed exploratorily; the reported associations are ecological and hypothesis-generating.
